status: Implementation plan; this file is not an available lesson
objective: Calculate signed work for constant and position-dependent forces and verify it against kinetic-energy change.
preparation: m01-l02 dot products and vector components
m02-l01 definite integrals, initial conditions, and reversals
m03-l01 net force and system choice
m03-l02 relative sliding for friction direction
teachingSequence: Define work by a named force as the integral of its component along a directed path, with joule units and signs.
Reduce a constant vector force to its dot product with displacement; distinguish displacement from traveled distance.
Evaluate affine, polynomial, piecewise, and spring force integrals with the correct limits and units of coefficients.
Parameterize a simple planar path and compare two paths for a position-dependent nonconservative force.
Derive the constant-mass particle work-energy theorem from F_net dot v; sum the work of all forces before using it.
Check endpoint and intermediate reachability; distinguish a finite turning point, asymptotic limiting point, and an exact rest equilibrium.
Explain when fixed constraints do zero work and how moving support or friction can do positive work in a selected inertial frame.
Connect instantaneous power F dot v to average work divided by elapsed time, without inferring elapsed time from energy alone.

workedFixtures.expected: Work=-5 J; reversing displacement reverses work.

workedFixtures.case: affine force with independent motion solution
workedFixtures.expected: Work=21 J, K0=4 J, Kfinal=25 J, speed=5 m/s. Independent solution x(t)=2(exp(t)-1), v(t)=2exp(t) reaches x=3 at ln(5/2) s.
Spring work=k(x0²-x1²)/2=0.75 J. The sign comes from the endpoints, not from adding unsigned areas.

workedFixtures.case: two paths through the same endpoints
workedFixtures.expected: Along y=x² from x=0 to2, W=8/3 J; along y=2x, W=4 J. A position-dependent force need not be conservative.
Normal work=+60 J and weight work=-60 J; net work zero. A normal force is not universally work-free.
Initial K=9 J; forward motion stops at x=3 m after 2 s. Formal endpoint candidate K(4)=-3 J is inaccessible.

workedFixtures.case: positive endpoint energy beyond a barrier
workedFixtures.expected: K(x)=(x-3)² J. The endpoint candidate is 9 J, but x(t)=3(1-exp(-t)) approaches x=3 asymptotically and cannot reach 6 on the stated motion.
Instantaneous power=8 W; the perpendicular portions of force do not contribute.

oracles: Independent dot products, geometric signed areas, and numerical quadrature
Differentiate force antiderivatives and kinetic-energy identities
Cross-check selected trajectories with independent acceleration solutions or converged integration
Zero work, reversed limits, orthogonal vectors, zero speed, negative candidate kinetic energy, and interior barriers
Reject units in numeric fields and invalid domains; accept equivalent exact answers

investigation.type: Energy along a proposed straight path with an explicit forward-motion feasibility check
investigation.assumptions: A constant-mass particle is constrained to a fixed horizontal straight guide that can supply transverse forces without work. The net along-guide force is A+B*x, where A=F*cos(theta), and all other along-guide forces are absent. Initial x=0 and nonnegative forward speed are stated. No time integration is displayed.
inputs: constant force magnitude F and angle theta from +x
investigation.feasibility: Do not report a real final speed from negative K. Search for the first zero of K in the proposed interval. A simple zero with negative slope is a finite turn; a double zero is an asymptotic limit. An exactly resting body with nonpositive initial forward force does not start along the proposed positive path, including the F(0)=0 equilibrium.
predictions: signed formal work along the proposed path
accessibleOutput: Signed force-position area plot with labeled scales
Kinetic-energy-versus-position plot with first limiting point
Keyboard controls and explicit units; exploratory controls reset
investigation.evidence: Compare positive, negative, and zero work; record a reversed or oblique-force prediction; demonstrate both a negative endpoint candidate and a positive endpoint beyond a barrier. Save one independent force/energy check and a domain explanation in notes.
investigation.boundary: A prescribed path integral can be calculated even if the body cannot reach its endpoint under the specified initial state and net force. Label formal work and actual reachable motion separately.
